title: Stamp 1: La Nouvelle Vague
welcome_lead: Earn your stamp by exploring the French New Wave cinema movement.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on the Nouvelle Vague, Truffaut, Godard, and 1959 cinema revolution.
final_note: You have collected the New Wave stamp.

concepts.def: French New Wave film movement starting in 1959, breaking classical cinema conventions.
Director of Les Quatre Cents Coups (1959), a defining New Wave film.
Director of A bout de souffle (1960), known for jump cuts and experimental style.
Influential film magazine where New Wave directors began as critics.
Idea that the director is the author of the film, expressed in la politique des auteurs.
Editing technique popularised by Godard, breaking continuity for stylistic effect.

walkthroughs.body_html: The movement began around 1959 with young critics from Cahiers du Cinema turning into directors. They rejected polished studio films, preferring location shooting, natural light, and personal stories.
Les Quatre Cents Coups (Truffaut, 1959) tells the story of troubled youth Antoine Doinel. A bout de souffle (Godard, 1960) revolutionised editing with jump cuts and a casual narrative style.
Le realisateur = director. Le scenario = screenplay. Le tournage = filming. La mise en scene = staging. Le plan = shot. Le montage = editing.
